rows.Description: Proposed mix of residential townhouses and low-rise employment uses. The proposal includes three blocks of 4-storey residential townhouse units along the south side of Judson Street, containing a total of 72 units, and two blocks of 3-storey commercial condominium units on the southerly portion of the site, containing a total of 28 units.
Proposed place of worship

Proposed development comprising of a 10 storey medical building and two 26 and 23 storey residential buildings and townhouses.  This development amalgamates 3 parcels of land in the Steeles-Redlea area.

Zoning By-law amendment to retain the existing six-storey heritage building on the western portion of the site and to develop a new, 20-storey tower on the eastern half of the site. The existing retail and commercial uses within the heritage building will be maintained and the proposed tower addition will contain retail uses at grade and office uses above. No vehicular parking is proposed.
The application proposes, on the northwest corner of the subject property, an 11-storey building with a 4-storey podium.

An Official Plan Amendment and Rezoning application has been submitted for the subject lands to permit the construction of a 38 Storey tower including an 11 storey base building.  The proposal would contain 584 residential units. The proposal also includes  1,582 square metres of retail space located on the 1st floor and 3,170 square metres of office uses located on the first and second floors. Three levels of underground parking containing 405 parking spaces are proposed.

The applicant proposes to  construct a place of worship consisting of prayer hall, gymnasium, indoor swimming pool, service area and meeting rooms. Two small zarees (display areas) a  mezzanine and ancillary service building are also proposed. The basement is intended to include office space for the religious organization, daycare, guest rooms and a recreational space.
Site plan approval application for the (demolition of existing 2 unit detached house and) construction of an 8 unit, four level condominium with an underground parking garage.

Zoning By-Law Amendment application to permit a 9-storey institutional building, containing 14,770 square metres of non-residential gross floor area. The proposal includes heritage conservation on the site.

INACTIVE Zoning By- Law Amendment Application to permit to permit a 10-storey mixed-use building, containing 60 rental dwelling units and 127 square metres of non-residential gross floor area.     This application is being reviewed and considered concurrently with a separate Official Plan Amendment application (File No. 24 248345 STE 19 OZ) for the same proposal.

The proposed development consists of eighteen (18) 4-storey townhouses comprising a total of 3,697 square metres on the subject site and a density of approximately 1.5 FSI. Each unit will contain three bedrooms and contain one parking space in an integral garage.  Access will be provided by way of a private lane that will run along 395 Leslie Street, and northsouth, parallel to the townhouses. THE OWNER HAS APPEALED THIS FILE TO THE OMB.  PLANNING RECEIVED A NEW CIRCULATION THAT IS BEFORE THE OMB ON SEPTEMBER 8, 2017, SHOWING 7 DETACHED DWELLINGS AND 4 TOWNHOUSE UNITS.

INACTIVE Site Plan Application for a 10-storey mixed-use building with a restaurant at grade and 14 residential units above. The development does not include any vehicular parking, but includes 2 short-term and 13 long-term bicycle parking spaces. Associated variances were approved by the Committee of Adjustment (File No. A0715/18TEY).
Proposal to construct a new gas station

Zoning By-law amendment to reduce the minimum lot frontage requirement from 21m to 15 m to enable the severance of the existing 5 lots into 12 new lots for single detached dwellings,  to allow for a reduced side yard building setback of 1.2 m on one side of the future dwellings,  and to permit a reduction in the minimum rear yard building setback to 7.5 m + 40% of lot depth where the lot depth is greater than 33.5 m.   The rear portions of the lands are proposed to be rezoned to Major Open Spaces (O) and conveyed into public ownership.  The total site area is approx. 2.37 ha.  Concurrent consent applications (file no.'s B003/12SC to B007/12SC inclusive) have also been filed.

The applicant proposes to construct a six-storey self-storage facility, having a gross floor area of 15,684 square metres and a height of 22.9 metres.  Fourteen parking spaces are proposed, one of which would be barrier-free.  Four bicycle parking spaces are proposed, one of which would be long-term and located inside the building.

To construct 21 three-storey townhouses at the rear of the property. The townhouses will have a height of 13.68 m and gross floor area of 2,498 m2. The existing six-storey rental apartment building containing 71 units will be maintained.
Proposed 13-storey mixed-use building with 85 residential units and at-grade retail. 87 underground parking spaces.

Revised development application as per Committee of Adjustment decisions. Floor area increased and number of storey's increased. SF April 7th, 2016. Site Plan approval application (Phase 2) to construct a mixed use development comprising a 23 and 19 storey condominium apartment building connected by 5 storey podium having a total gross floor area of 48,335 square metres including 653 square metres of grade related retail space and a 4-level   underground parking containing 682 spaces.
INACTIVE Development of vacant land for a concrete batching plant and ancillary office trailers.
The proposal is for a one-storey convenience store with a drive-thru, a car-wash and a gas-bar on Parcel A and a 4-storey hotel (140 rooms) and a one-storey restaurant building on Parcel B.

Two-storey, 5,461 square metre Public Community Centre including an 846 square metre Child Care Centre and 533 square metre Pool Pavilion building. The application also includes general parkland landscape enhancements and amenity replacements including a playground and two multi-purpose sports courts.
To demolish the existing industrial building and construct a one-storey multi unit industrial building with a GFA of 13,579 square metres.
INACTIVE Proposed 3 storey building with a gym in the basement, offices on first through third floors, banquet hall on basement and first floor.
third floor addition to Avondale School
Application to permit new 6,468 square mtre two-storey elementary school with daycare. The existing elementary school will be demolished and replace by this proposed development.

Proposed amendments to the Official Plan and Zoning By-laws to permit the development of a 6-storey residential building (84 units) with a total gross floor area of 6,685.07 square metres. A total of 113 parking spaces are proposed (surface parking lot and 2 level underground parking garage).

Zoning by-law amendment to permit a 10-storey (32.45 metres, excluding mechanical penthouse) residential mixed-use building with 126 units and retail at grade.  This application was scheduled to be considered by Toronto and East York Community Council at its October meeting. The item was deferred to February TEYCC to accommodate review of additional changes. For the latest plans and statistics, please see the materials uploaded on November 17, 2020 and later.

Zoning by law amendment applicaiton to permit the redevelopmetn of the land for a new 7 unit infill townhouse development (Freehold) serviced by common element driveway leading to private parking to the rear of each unit.  Each unit to front onto a municipal street..  Seperate application for common element condo to follow.

Revised Application Submitted on December 15, 2017: The Applicant, Belleterre Real Estate Partners Limited, has submitted a revised application for Site Plan Control, which proposes the development of a 5-storey, 13,447 m2, self-storage warehouse (Storage Warehouse, Class A) over two phases of construction. Loading docks for the proposed storage use will be provided and will be located internal to the proposed building. A 371 m2 Designer's Studio is proposed to be located on the ground floor of the 5-storey building. A total of 40 parking spaces, 6 bicycle parking spaces, and 4 loading spaces are proposed to serve the development. The site has a total area of 18,245 m2; however, the development will be located only on the northern portion of the site, which maintains an area of 6,638 m2. Please note that the site is subject to the Lower Don Special Policy Area. Also note that the approval for this site plan now rests with the Ontario Municipal Board (OMB). The OMB issued a decision on July 4, 2016 (Case # MM150067) allowing the development to proceed in its proposed location, and issued a subsequent oral decision on July 27, 2017, requesting to resolve this matter within 20 business days of final site plan submission to City staff. As Planning and Legal staff have been directed to respond to the OMB with a full and final NOAC, please ensure your comments include final pre- and post-approval conditions.
To permit 5 freehold townhouse dwelling units and 2 single detached dwelling units together with a private access road.

Rezoning application for a three-storey plus mezzanine residential condominium containing seven dwelling units. The building height is 12.19 metres. The total GFA of the project is 1000.26 square metres.

To redevelop the site with 2 and 3-storey retail podium base and 38 storey residential tower above (40 storeys total).  A total of 333 residential units are proposed along with 4132 square metres of retail floor area.  Parking will be provided in a 5 level underground parking structure.

Zoning by-law Amendment application to facilitate the development of the site for a 15-storey, plus mezzanine non-residential building having a gross floor area of approximately 18343 square metres.  46 parking spaces will be provided on the lot, located within a below grade parking structure.

Note that this tower was one of two office towers approved through a rezoning application for the larger (former Toronto Sun) property at 333 King Street East, file no 12 144494 STE 28 OZ and site-specific Bylaw 818-2013 (with amending Bylaw 401-2014 and CofA Decision dated Dec 10, 2014, file no A0974/14TEY),

OPA and Rezoning application for a new 11 storey mixed use building - 109 residential suites - 3 levels below grade parking - 125 bicycle parking spaces - 4 retail units at grade.

5-storey commercial office building with ground floor retail and a drive-thru restaurant (15,954.7 m2 of GFA); Building B: 1-storey retail building (1,408.5 m2); and 293 parking spaces (159 surface and 134 below grade).

This Site Plan Control application (Phase 2) proposes to construct a 14- storey residential (Life Lease) apartment building (Building A) and a one-storey mixed-use building addition to the existing community centre (Building C). The portion of the above-grade proposed 5-storey retirement building (Building B) would be constructed under the Phase 3 development of the site. Only the below grade portion of Building B will be constructed as part of the Phase 2 development. A Section 37 Agreement was registered for the subject site on May 17, 2013. A site-specific Zoning By-law 152-2011 (OMB) regulates the site.

Proposal to redevelop the existing single family dwelling with five, two-storey townhouse units fronting onto Danforth Road.  The townhouses will have access to parking/garages from the rear of the lots off of Mack Avenue.

As such,  rezoning application 13 247713 ESC 44 OZ is amended to permit 26 parking spaces on site and remove the parking from the hydro corridor, A concurrent site plan application 13 205126 ESC 44 SA is also being processed with the rezoning applications.

Rental Building "A" known as 40 Meadowglen Place. Proposed new mixed use commercial residential building approximately 56, 418.00 square metres.  The proposal contemplates a podium consisting of primarily retail commercial uses and a food store.  Residential units are proposed with a top floor restaurant in the northern most tower.

A proposal to construct a 7 storey mixed use building containing 142 residential units with commercial at grade.  A total of 151 parking spaces will be provided in 2 levels underground.  Also see Site Plan Application 12 138115 STE 31 SA [updated December 21, 2012]

Bousfields Inc. has submitted an application for Zoning By-law Amendment.  The application proposes three mixed-use buildings with heights of 25, 30 and 37 storeys. The proposed development would be deployed in 2 phases with phase 1 consisting of the 37-storey building and phase 2 consisting of the 25 and 30 storeys buildings. The application proposes 935 residential units with a mix of unit types resulting in a residential gross floor area of 67,992 square metres.     The application also proposes 522 square metres of retail/commercial uses and an overall floor space index of 7.36 times. A total of 742 vehicular and 714 bicycle parking spaces and 3 type G and 6 type C loading spaces would be provided. The proposal would provide a new 930 square-metre public park at the western portion of the site, pedestrian connections and privately-owned publicly accessible open spaces. A related Subdivision Application No. 21 201457 ESC 21 SB to create 4 new blocks has also been submitted by the applicant.

Planned as new inclusive, compact and complete community that is walkable and well served by transit and active transportation. The Neighbourhood is intended to be developed over phases with a broad range and mix of uses, built forms, densities, housing and unit types and tenures (including affordable and seniors options), all supported by an existing higher order transit and existing and planned community services and facilities. The District Plan for the William Baker Neighbourhood includes development blocks at the south end proposed for a mix of high/mid and low-rise residential as well as mixed use blocks at the intersection of Keele Street and Sheppard Avenue, to create a Neighbourhood Focus at that gateway to the community featuring commercial uses and parks, in a location well served by transit. Building heights in this area are proposed to range from 4 to 20 storeys. Residential blocks proposed in the north portion, which will be developed through subsequent phases, provide for similar heights in the range of 4 to 20 storeys, with potential for some taller elements near the Downsview Park subway/GO station hub. Of great importance to the future of the Neighbourhood is preservation and enhancement of the woodlot. It will be a central feature of the new community and further enhanced with additional parkland being added around its edges as contemplated by the Secondary Plan. Additionally, a park at the southern end of the Neighbourhood is proposed to feature a new pedestrian/cycling bridge that will provide a convenient link to Downsview Park to the south.

A total of 274 bicycle parking spaces are proposed including 239 long term and 35 short term spaces. The proposed development provides a total GFA of 22,416.70 square metres and a FSI of 11.23. Additionally, the proposed development provides 637.90 square metres of indoor amenity space and 632.40 square metres of outdoor amenity space.

OPA & Rezoning Application proposes the development of an 14-storey residential building. The building will provide a total of 139 residential units, being a mix of 1-bedroom, 2-bedroom, and 3-bedroom units. A paved access from Sheppard Ave W will be provided, leading to 1 level of below-grade parking, providing a total of 28 parking spaces; as well as 104 bicycle parking spaces. The proposed development provides a total GFA of 9596 square metres and a FSI of 7.8. Additionally, the proposed development provides 308 square metres of indoor amenity space and 248 square metres of outdoor amenity space.
Zoning By-law Amendment for a 45-storey mixed-use building. The building will contain 379 residential units, 9 of which are rental replacement units, with commercial at grade.

Proposed redevelopment of the existing Petro Canada gas station located at 800 York Mills Rd. The redevelopment includes the construction of new gas pumps and canopy, a new convenience store/quick-service KFC restaurant with an associated drive-through facility, and comprehensive  landscaping throughout the property. The existing car wash facilities and existing fuel tank nest will remain a part of the development.

OPA and Zoning By-law Amendment application proposes the development of a 6-storey retirement residence. The building will provide a total of 141 residential units, being a mix of independant living, assisted living, and memory care units. A paved access from Bayview Ave along the southern property line will be provided, leading to 1 level of below-grade parking, providing a total of 54 parking spaces; as well as 25 bicycle parking spaces. The proposed development provides a total GFA of 14,454.06 square metres and a FSI of 2.61. Additionally, the proposed development provides 1,515.65 square metres of indoor amenity space and 1,063.68 square metres of outdoor amenity space.

A Zoning Bylaw Amendment Application that proposes the development of a 10-storey mixed-use building providing residential and commercial use at grade. The building will provide a total of 77 residential units, being a mix of studio, 1-bedroom, 2-bedroom, 3-bedrooms. The building will also provide 2 retail units at grade. A paved access from Sunrise Ave will be provided, leading to 3 levels of below-grade parking, providing a total of 41 parking spaces; as well as 88 bicycle parking spaces. The proposed development provides a total GFA of 5,574.34 square metres and a FSI of 5.30. Additionally, the proposed development provides 162.39 square metres of indoor amenity space and 180.90 square metres of outdoor amenity space.

Site Plan Control Application proposes the removal of an existing tennis court to construct a four court pickleball zone. This zone would feature a seasonal dome (incl. concrete grade beam). Fire route access and main site access will remain untouched.

Proposal for a new 9-storey long-term care home with approximately 512 beds on the southern portion of the site and retaining the existing building on the north portion of the site.    Please note that the applicant intends to submit a severance application that will sever the vacant southern portion of the site, which is the subject of the zoning application, from the existing building on the north portion of the site.

Proposed construction of two 12-storey mixed-use buildings in the north and south ends of the subject site. The 14-storey building, inclusive of its ground floor non-residential component, will be retained.

A City-initiated Official Plan & Zoning By-law Amendment application for a 30-storey apartment building with 301 rental units (including 61 affordable rental units) and an 8-storey building with 81 supportive housing units. No development is proposed in the existing park located at 801 Wellington Street West (Wellington Park). This site is part of the Toronto Builds program.

Rezoning Application proposing a new replacement building for the existing 252-bed Long Term Care Home to be built on the existing surface parking lot before demolition of the existing building to provide for an additional seniors retirement home and rental apartment building in two components of 15 and 16 storeys.

Proposed 13-storey residential rental building and one level of underground parking. It provides a total of 259 units designed to accommodate housefhold of varying sizes, incomes, ages and with varying social needs. It has a combination of Affordale Rental and Rent-Controlled Rental Homes. Min. 30% of units at affordable rents; Min 20% of units meet accessibility standards. The development subjects to RHSP program,  ARRCHI stream, and PDRS stream.
Zoning By-law Amendment for an 8-storey residential building with 77 apartment dwelling units.

Rezoning for a 31 storey residential (condominium) apartment building containing 297 dwelling units. Block 8, Plan 66M-2460. Zoning for entire plan of subdivision lands required to be amended as zoning applies collectively.

Proposal for a mixed use building with 37-storey and 39-storey tower elements with a 7-storey shared podium, separate 39-storey residential building with a 6-storey podium, a public park and a privately accessible open area are also proposed.  Total of 920 residential units, 713 sq.m of office, 607 sq.m. of retail, 994 vehicle parking spaces and 691 bicycle parking spaces are proposed. Existing 13-storey office and 1-storey parking structure to remain.

The revised re-zoning and Official Plan amendment applications propose a 6-storey (19.65 m) residential building consisting of 4 two-storey grade-related townhouse units and 67 apartment units, for a total of 71 units. A total of 5,931 square metres of residential GFA is proposed, equating to a FSI of 2.56 times the lot area.The revised applications propose a 232 square metre on-site parkland dedication along the western limit of the site. Site access is proposed via a 7.2 metre wide driveway off Hendon Ave which leads to the loading area and ramp to the UG garage. A total of 44 parking spaces are proposed within one level of UG parking.

The proposed redevelopment of this site includes a new hotel and performance venue that will attract local, national, and international visitors. The proposed entertainment venue is a tiered modern concert venue, which can seat up to 5,500 patrons. The program is intended to host concerts, esports  events, conventions, corporate events, product launches, and awards shows. The proposed hotel building is a 32-storey, 111.92-metre-tall mixed-use tower with approximately 370 guest rooms.

Official Plan Amendment (OPA) to re-designate the subject site from Core Employment Areas to Mixed Use Areas to permit future mixed-use development. The OPA would also introduce a new Site and Area Specific Policy that mandates a minimum of 3,150 square metres of gross floor area dedicated to activities related to film, television, and digital media production.

Proposed mid-rise self-storage facility of nine (9) storeys and 34.30 metres in height. Vehicular access is off of Coxwell Avenue, which leads to a covered customer service, parking and loading areas, including ten (10) parking spaces, two (2) loading spaces, and three (3) short-term bicycle parking spaces. The proposed mid-rise self-storage facility has a building area of 13,360.84 square metres.

Province submitted a Transit-Oriented Community proposal for Martin Grove (Martin Grove TOC).  Located at the north east corner of Martin Grove Road and Eglinton Ave. West adjacent to Eglinton Crosstown West Extension - Martin Grove Station.

keyword_matches.Description: Zoning by-law amendment to permit a 10-storey (32.45 metres, excluding mechanical penthouse) residential mixed-use building with 126 units and retail at grade.  This application was scheduled to be considered by Toronto and East York Community Council at its October meeting. The item was deferred to February TEYCC to accommodate review of additional changes. For the latest plans and statistics, please see the materials uploaded on November 17, 2020 and later.

To permit the development of an 18-storey mixed use building containing 204 residential units and approximately 1425 m2 of ground floor and mezzanine level retail.  The proposed building would have a 9-storey base building and the total building height would be 53 metres excluding mechanical.  Twelve townhouses are propsed to face Lanark Avenue

INACTIVE Proposal for a 3 storey addition above the existing one storey office building. The existing basement is to be converted into a parking level and the existing roof is to be enclosed to create a mechanical level with three additional storey's above to be used as office space, resulting in a total of 5 storeys (21.6 m including 3rd floor mechanical level) and GFA of 4,624.2 square metres.
Construct an apartment building with 3 below grade parking levels; 14 storeys of residential and 1 storey mechanical on the roof. See PPR 17-155343 ZPR

Site Plan Application for the second phase of the Newtonbrook Plaza development.  Block 2 proposes a total gross floor area of 66,838.9 square metres, consisting of 63,152.3 square metres of residential GFA and 3,628.0 square metres of commercial GFA.  The proposed mixed use building would contain two towers on a shared podium. One tower will be 34 storeys (106.3 metres excluding the mechanical penthouse) and the other proposed tower would be 40 storeys (123.5 metres excluding the mechanical penthouse). A total of 856 residential units are proposed with 543 vehicular parking spaces.  A new community centre and child care centre are also proposed as part of Phase 2.

6-storey residential development, excluding mechanical penthouse containing 143 units with a 3-storey townhouse building element containing 18 units, indoor amenity areas (228 square metres) and outdoor amenity areas (322 square metres)

Proposed 12-storey (45.1 metres including the mechanical penthouse) mixed-use building containing 80 dwelling units and 221 square metres of retail. The total gross floor area is 5,648 square metres and the site density is 7.3 times the area of the lot. Two levels of underground parking are proposed with 19 parking spaces for residents and a total of 84 bicycle parking spaces.

9-storey, plus roof-top mechanical mid-rise building containing 80 (+ 1 guest suite) residential units with a total gross floor area of approximately 8 092 square metres and an associated two level, below-grade parking structure containing a total of 87 vehicle parking spaces, 63 bicycle parking spaces, mechanical rooms, elevator shaft, lockers and other uses

Revised Application Submitted April 10, 2017: The Applicant, 1177 Danforth Avenue Ltd., has submitted rezoning and site plan applications that propose to develop the site, municipally known as 1177 Danforth Avenue, with a 9 storey mixed-use residential condominium building with a total height of 29.75 m (31.25 m including mechanical penthouse). The proposed building consists of a total gross floor area (GFA) of 7,401.3 m2, which includes 92 residential condominium units, above 722.00 m2 of retail space at grade. The total FSI is 4.2 times the lot area. The Applicant is also proposing 66 vehicle parking spaces and 115 bicycle parking spaces to be placed at-grade and within two levels of below grade parking.

The proposal is for an 11-storey mixed-use building (35.85 metres in height, excluding the mechanical penthouse) with retail at grade and residential units above. The development includes an underground parking structure. The total proposed Gross Floor Area (GFA) is 35,112 square metres, with 537 units, 349 vehicular parking spaces, and 538 bicycle parking spaces.

The proposal is for an 11-storey mixed-use building (35.85 metres in height, excluding the mechanical penthouse) with retail at grade and residential units above. The development includes an underground parking structure. The total proposed Gross Floor Area (GFA) is 19,422 square metres, with 292 units, 178 vehicular parking and 296 bicycle parking.

Zoning By-law Amendment for a 23-storey (98.6 metres including the mechanical penthouse) non-residential building with retail at-grade and office above. The listed heritage property at 460 King Street West is proposed to be retained while the facade of the listed heritage property at 468 King Street is to be retained. Concurrent SA application: 22 138739 STE 10 SA

Original proposal for a 4-storey, 70 unit residential development with 68 underground parking spaces. Application has been appealed to the OMB and has been revised in accordance with the following: a reduction in the number of units from 70 to 42 and a shift from traditional apartment house dwelling units to back-to-back stacked townhouse units; a decrease in the proposed building coverage; the addition of a communal outdoor landscaped amenity area, doubling the overall amount of soft landscaping on the site; a shortened driveway due to a proposed car lift in replacement of the previously proposed car ramp; an increase in setbacks along the Finch and Elmview Avenue frontages and rear yard; removal of the previously proposed rooftop mechanical units; better integration of waste management facilities.

Zoning By-law Amendment application to permit the redevelopment of the site with a mixed-use building comprised of 12 storeys fronting King Street West containing ground floor retail and office uses above, and a 15-storey residential building fronting Morrison Street. The total height of both portions of the building will be 50 metres, including mechanical elements. Loading access will be off of a public lane north of the site and vehicular access to a below grade garage will be off of Brant Street.

Official Plan and Zoning by Law Amendment application to permit the re-development of the lands for the purposes of a new mixed use building. The application proposes to retain the front portion of the existing heritage building (Bank Building) on the premises.  Included in the proposal is a 60-storey (204 metre) residential tower containing 694 dwelling units to the rear of the heritage building.  The proposed podium is 9-storey's containing the lobby to be located within the heritage building, above grade parking (floors 3 to 8), amenity uses (floors 9 and 10) and retail uses at grade in the area currently used as private open space adjacent the heritage building on the north side.  There are 113 above grade parking spaces proposed.  One below grade level is proposed to include mechanical and service areas and bicycle parking.

Zoning by-law amendment application to facilitate the redevelopment of the site with a 61-storey, 188.3 metre tall  (196.8 metres including the mechanical penthouse) mixed-use building. A total of 813 dwelling units are proposed along with ground floor retail, a community agency space, a paramedic post and a mid-block connection.

Original rezoning application submitted for a mixed-use development consisting of two residential towers at 45 and 54 storeys in height with a 9-10 storey podium. The development proposes a total gross floor area of 90,700 square metres and will feature 1,304 dwelling units above a 1 storey of street-related retail space. The original proposal frames a public park on the south side of the block. The second submission proposed one 54-storey tower (181 metres) located at the north east corner of the site with 681 units, retail at grade and office in floor 2 and 3. Access to below grade parking and loading is proposed from St. Luke Lane. A public parking facility is also proposed below grade. The proposal also includes an expanded park space from Wellesley Street to Breadalbane Street. Resubmission April 2, 2014 adding in the parcel of land on the east side of St Luke Lane, reducing the area of the, increasing the area of the park, the tower height proposed is 60 storyes (194 metres including mechanical penthouse), revising the gross floor area, increasing the number of units to 742.  The area of the proposed park has been increased to 5,382 sq.m.

Proposed development of a 9-storey (plus mechanical penthouse) residential development. The proposed development will result in 10,144 m2 of gross floor area, resulting with a Floor Space Index of 3.58 across the Subject Lands.The proposal will consist of approximately 148 residential units consisting of 24 studio units (16%), 69 onebedroom units (46%), 40 two-bedroom units (27%), and 15 three-bedroom units (10%). A total of 73 parking spaces are proposed including 14 retail surface car parking spaces with the remaining spaces provided within one underground level including 5 accessible parking spaces.

Zoning By-law Amendment to facilitate redevelopment of the site with a new 9-storey, mixed-use building (29.5 metres excluding the mechanical penthouse): 898 square metres of retail space  and 4,917 square metres of residential space containing 76 dwelling units.

Application to amend the Zoning By-law to permit a retirment home in a 10-storey (38 metres, excluding mechanical penthouse) building with a retail store (887 square metres) at grade. A total of 146 bed-sitting rooms and 53 vehicular parking spaces are proposed.

Redevelopment of a 620 square metre (0.15 acre) property located on the southeast corner of Camden Street and Brant Street, municipally known as 49 and 51 Camden Street (the subject site), for a 13-storey hotel with a partially integrated mechanical penthouse. The new Ace Hotel would consist of 130 hotel suites, a lower level restaurant, a gymnasium, a ground floor hotel lobby and various hotel-related meeting rooms. A penthouse lounge and outdoor terrace would be located on the 13th floor.  A total gross floor area of 7,918 square metres is proposed.

The Site is proposed to be redeveloped with a new 28-storey (plus mechanical penthouse) mixed-use building. A total gross floor area of 18,392 square metres is proposed, consisting of 18,145 square metres of residential uses and 247 square metres of grade-related retail uses.

Zoning By-law Amendment to permit a 31-storey hotel tower with a total building height of 115.1 m (inclusive of mechanical penthouse). A total of 392 hotel suites are proposed with a total GFA of approximately 26,744 square metres. The existing heritage Rack House D building is proposed to be incorporated as part of the proposal.

Zoning By-law Amendment application to permit a mixed-use development including two buildings, 37 and 42 storeys in height (131.0 metres and 145.2 metres, respectively, including mechanical penthouses). Proposed uses include two levels of retail, seven levels of office space, a daycare, the replacement of the existing movie theatre, an on-site publicly accessible privately owned open space and 693 residential units. The total gross floor area proposed is 80,334m2, consisting of 49,983m2 of residential floor area, and 30,351m2 of non-residential floor area.  Two levels of below grade parking are proposed with 231 vehicle and 829 bicycle parking spaces. (Enacted as by-law 949-2022. Third-party appeal received.)

Proposed amendments to the Official Plan and Zoning By-laws to permit a total of 499 residential units within a 29-storey (93 m, including mechanical penthouse) apartment building with a 5-storey (13.5 m) podium and a mid-rise building stepping upto 12-storeys (41 m, including mechanical penthouse).

Site Plan application to allow for the construction of a new commercial office building. The proposed building will be 11 storeys (44.86 metres) in height, excluding the mechanical penthouse. The proposed gross floor area of the building is 16,736.56 square metres, consisting of 16,544.91 square metres of office space and 191.65 square metres of ground floor retail uses.

OLT Approved Application to Amend the Zoning By-law to permit the re-development of the site with a 50-storey (157 metre tall including the mechanical penthouse) mixed-use building containing retail, restaurant and office uses within the first 5 floors and 403 residential units above.  A total of 146 parking spaces are proposed within a six level underground parking garage. Portions of the heritage buildings on the site are proposed to be retained and integrated into the podium.  This application is being reviewed in conjunction with Site Plan application (File No. 22- 204481 STE 10 SA).

The proposal is for the redevelopment of the existing 6.7 acre site with a total density of 3.8 times the site area. The proposed includes 3,633 m2 of retail commercial space, a network of new public and private streets, two new privately-owned publicly accessible open spaces and a 3,378 m2 off-site parkland dedication. The proposal includes 4 new residential buildings (containing 1,279 units) ranging in height from 16 to 28 storeys (57.5 to 93 metres, excluding mechanical penthouses).

Application to permit the construction of a new 22-storey mixed use building. Retail and commercial uses are proposed in the first 2-storeys, with a total of 202 residential dwelling units above.  The proposal would have an overall building height of approximately 70 metres to the top of the main roof (plus mechanical penthouse).  The new building will contain three levels of underground parking accommodating 70 vehicular spaces and accessed from Douglas Campbell Lane.  214 bicycle parking spaces are proposed as part of this application.

The proposed development consists of a mixed-use building with 36 storey and 29 storey towers (respectively 116.2 m and 98.7 m in height excl. mechanical penthouses) 413 sqm of retail at grade, a 12,374 sqm multi-storey self-storage building as a future phase, and a 1,146 m2 public park.     Related applications: Zoning Amendment (21 236250 WET 03 OZ), Subdivision (21 236297 WET 03 SB), Site Plan (21 252097 WET 03 SA)

A proposed nine-storey (with amenity space and mechanical only on the 9th floor) mixed-use, mid-rise building.  There are 80 residential units, 196 square metres of commercial space on the ground floor and 79 parking spaces on three underground levels.  The total GFA is approximately 6493 square metres, resulting in a density of 3.47 times the lot area.

The development applications would permit a 33-storey mixed use building with height  of 106.1 metres (112.1 inclusive of the mechanical penthouse), containing 370 dwelling units, 324 square metres of non-residential space, 63 parking spaces and 434 bicycle parking spaces within three levels of underground parking. The total proposed gross floor area is 22,529 square metres, resulting in a density of 16.7 times the area of the lot.
Develop a 6 storey Mixed-Use building. Residential Apartment Condominium on the upper 5 floors, with Commercial space on the first floor. Mechanical and outdoor amenities on 7th floor.

Official Plan and Zoning By-Law Amendment to permit an 8-storey apartment building fronting onto Dufferin Street and 4 storey townhouses fronting onto Boland Lane.  The height of the building would be 25.1 metres (excluding Mechanical Penthouse), and it would contain 78 dwelling units and a total of 43 parking spaces within an underground garage. A total of 9 townhouses are proposed at the rear of the site.  This application is being reviewed with the Zoning By-law Amendment application at 1494-1502 Dundas St. West (File No. 19 101840 STE 09 OZ).

Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment application for a 9-storey (30.2 metres including mechanical penthouse), 188-bed (160 dwelling rooms and 28 dwelling units) student residence with a food hall on the ground floor.

The proposal is to construct a new 49-storey mixed-use building with three levels of underground parking. The ground level includes a shared residential and office lobby as well as retail and commercial uses fronting onto Danforth Avenue and a portion of Pape Avenue. Office uses are proposed from the third to fifth floors and the residential use is proposed from the sixth to 49th floors. Above the 49th floor is the mechanical penthouse and an indoor and outdoor amenity space. Additional indoor amenity spaces are located on the sixth and seventh floors and an additional outdoor amenity space is proposed on the sixth floor with access to the indoor amenity space. The proposal includes a total of 496 dwelling units, 29,756 sq. m (320,291 sq. ft.) of residential gross floor area (GFA) and 4,743 sq. m (51,053 sq. ft.) of non-residential GFA.
Zoning By-law Amendment application for a 29-storey mixed-use building (86.25m including mechanical penthouse) with 576 sq. m of retail and 328 residential units.

An application to amend City of Toronto Zoning By-law No. 438-86 to permit a mixed use development with a 23-storey tower and a 52-storey tower containing 776 residential condominium units on a shared 7-storey podium.  The podium would contain retail uses at grade and five storeys of above grade parking with 185 parking spaces for residents and 47 parking spaces for visitors. Above grade parking is required because the TTC subway tunnel runs the length of the property. The height of the towers would be 80 and 174 metres (including mechanical penthouse).  Driveway access and servicing would be from Maitland Place. The lobbies for the residential condominiums would be on Alexander Street and Maitland Street.

Proposed six-storey addition (33 metres, including mechanical penthouse) to the existing Woodsworth College institutional building, consisting of approximately 3,767 square metres of new institutional floor area.

The proposed development consists of a new 11-storey (plus mechanical penthouse) mixed-use building along Kingston Road, with flexible work space for artists and musicians on the ground floor and residential uses above, along with a row of townhouses oriented along a pedestrian walkway on the Annis-fronting property. Parking is proposed to be accommodated in one underground level and above-grade on levels 1 through 4, which would be screened from view by dwelling units. The existing buildings on the subject site are proposed to be demolished.
Zoning By-law Amendment Application to permit a 7-storey (22.5 metre, including mechanical penthouse) residential building with a gross floor area of approximately 1360 square metres.

Zoning by-law amendment to permit a 12-storey mixed-use building (plus mezannine and 2-storey mechanical penthouse) with 293 residential units and 614 square metres of retail, comprising a total GFA of 28,932 square metres. 184 vehicle parking spaces are proposed. The two existing commercial buildings would be demolished.

The applicant proposes to construct a 30-storey mixed-use building which contains 572 residential units as well as a total of 6,399.45 square metres of retail space on the ground floor, mezzanine, second floor and concourse level, and 2,843.78 square metres of office space on the third floor.  The height of the building to the main roof is 101.6 metres (107.5 metres including mechanical penthouse).  A total of 241 vehicular parking spaces are provided in a 4-level below-grade garage and 627 bicycle parking spaces are provided.  The floor space index proposed is 15.84.
To construct a 38-storey (117.5 metres, plus 6 metre mechanical) residential tower containing 385 dwelling units.

Revised Zoning  Amendment application to redevelop the site with a 24-storey mixed-use building with a height of 76.8 meters (82.8 metres including the mechanical penthouse). A non-residential gross floor area of 351 square metres is proposed along with 226 residential units.

Application to amend the Official Plan and Zoning By-law to allow for the devleopment of a new 9-storey mixed-use building (31.20 metres plus 5.0 metre mechanical penthouse). The proposal contains a total gross floor area of 9,699.4 square metres, including 9,160.6 square metres of residential gross floor area and 447.6 square metres of retail/commercial gross floor area, and 91.2 square metres of community space, resulting in an overall density of 5.2 FSI. A total of 117 new residential units are proposed including 81 one-bedroom units (69%), 23 twobedroom units (20%) and 13 three-bedroom units (11%).

Zoning amendment application to allow the redevelopment of the site with a non-residential building with a height of 10 storeys fronting King Street West (43.45 metres including the mechanical penthouse) and 12 storeys fronting Adelaide Street West and Portland Street (51.95 metres including the mechanical penthouse). The heritage buildings on the site will be conserved and  incorporated into the development.  This development has been approved in principle by the OLT (File No. PL171510).

Zoning Amendment Application to permit the re-development of the site with an addition overtop of and behind the existing heritage building, increasing the height of the existing building to a total of 9-storeys (36.5 metres to the top of the building and 41.5 metres to the top of the mechanical penthouse). The existing 4-storey heritage building is proposed to be incorporated into the development. The development would have a gross floor area of 5,417 square metres, would include 9 bicycle spaces, zero parking spaces, 1Type B and 1 Type C loading space.

The City has received an application to amend the Zoning By-law to allow a 15-storey (51.1 metres plus a 3.7-metre mechanical penthouse) mixed-use building with retail at-grade, 143 dwelling units, 33 vehicle parking spaces in a below grade garage, and 180 bicycle parking spaces. The application was appealed to the OLT by the applicant on November 5, 2021.

This is a substantially amended Zoning Amendment application submitted to address City concerns regardng the previous proposal for a 56-storey residential building.  The application has been appealed to the Ontario Municipal Board (OMB).  The revised proposal is for a 23-storey commerical building with retail and office uses with an overall height (including the mechanical penthouse) of 103.5 metres.  Vehicular parking is proposed to be located below grade, with 31 spaces to be provided in a four level automated parking system.

Rezoning proposal for a 12-storey residential building, inclusive of a rooftop mechanical/amenity floor, and residential uses at-grade at the rear and above. The proposed building will contain a total Gross Floor Area (GFA) of approximately 18,350.1 sq m (197,520.6 sq ft.), with a proposed density of 5.0 FSI. 287 residential dwelling units and 158 vehicle parking spaces are proposed.
The City has received an application to amend the Zoning By-law to allow a 40-storey (123.1 metres plus a 9.75-metre mechanical penthouse) mixed-use building with ground level retail.

This application is for an Official Plan Amendment ONLY, not a rezoning or site plan application.   The proposal is to amend the Official Plan through a site specific policy that will recognize the potential future redevelopment of the site with a building up to 11 storeys in height (plus mechanical penthouse) while maintaining the heritage cottage in the rear of the property.   Please note that this applicant has appealed the Broadview Avenue Official Plan Amendment.

INACTIVE Current May/June 2024 proposal - 12-storey residential buidling containing 80 rental dwelling units (including 20 rental replacement units), 12 parking spaces and 85 bike parking spaces    Jan 2024 Proposal - 12-storey (40.6 metres including mechanical penthouse) residential building containing 80 rental residential dwelling units (including 20 rental replacement), 12 parking spaces and 85 bike parking spaces.     REVISED proposal (June 2022) for a 12-storey (40.6 metres including mechanical penthouse) residential building containing 80 rental residential dwelling units (including 20 rental replacement) and 16 parking spaces, and with a gross floor area of 5,517 square metres, which is a floor space index of 5.74 times the lot area.

Revised Zoning Amendment application to redevelop the site with a 15-storey mixed-use building containing 125 residential units, commercial uses at grade and 25 parking spaces below grade. The building will have a height of 45 metres, including the sunken mechanical penthouse.

The application proposes to amend Zoning By-law 569-2013 at 632-652 Northcliffe Boulevard to permit a residential building 129 metres in height (38-storeys including mechanical penthouse), with a maximum of 30,250 square metres of gross floor area and 11 rental replacement housing units. A related Rental Housing Demolition and Conversion application (22 218880 STE 12 RH) under Section 111 of the City of Toronto Act, 2006 (Chapter 667 of the Municipal Code) has been submitted to permit the demolition.

Zoning By-law amendment for two mixed use buildings and one residential building in addition to the existing residential building on the property.  Building A is a 36-storey tower (112.8 metres) with a six-storey podium, 432 residential units, and 486 m2 of retail.  Building B is a 32-storey tower (108.3 metres) with a six-storey podium, 355 units, and 387 m2 of retail.  Building C is an 8-storey building with 9th amenity/mechanical level (33.0 metres including mechanical), and 105 residential units.    In total, the Subject Site will accommodate 1,151 residential dwelling units, including 892 new apartment dwelling units and 259 retained rental apartment units.

Proposed 32-storey apartment building with a 4-storey podium.  Building height  to the top of the mechanical penthouse would be 102.45 metres. The project would have a Gross Floor Area of 17,773. sq m

Site Plan Control application for proposed 8-storey + mechanical mixed use building containing 60 residential units and 238 square metres of retail space on the ground floor.     Proposal has been revised to from 54 units and 180 square metres of retail space with additional massing at the rear of the building. A total of 29 vehicle parking spaces are proposed, 1 of which for visitors.

Zoning By-Law Amendment to permit an 8-storey mixed-use building fronting onto Dundas Street West. The height of the building would be 25.15 metres plus mechanical, and it would contain a total of 48 dwelling units, a 397 square metre retail unit at grade on Dundas Street West and a total of 18 stacked parking spaces accessed at grade from the rear laneway.  The loading space is proposed to be shared across the laneway with the proposal at 646 Dufferin Street.

Application for Zoning By-Law amendment to permit a new 51 storey mixed-use tower (162.5 metres plus a 7.5 metre mechanical penthouse). The application proposes to retain the facades of the heritage buildings on Yonge St.  A total of 399 residential dwelling units and 431square metres of non-residential gross floor area is proposed.

Zoning by-law amendment application for two towers: a 48-storey tower (156.25 metres including mechanical penthouse) and a 40-storey tower (130.15 metres including mechanical penthouse) containing 899 residential units on a 6 storey podium including  two levels of retail space, and  225 underground parking spaces. The application proposes to demolish proposed heritage properties at 350 and 352  Adelaide Street West, and 118 Peter Street.

The City received an application to amend the Zoning By-law to permit a new high-rise residential building in the northwest corner of a 1.26 hectare site with two existing high-rise rental apartment buildings.
